previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of gastroparesis, J-tube placement, and Nissen fundoplication was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea after eating ham, which triggered a flare of her chronic condition. She reported worsening symptoms over the prior week, including daily vomiting and abdominal discomfort. Initial labs were stable, and imaging confirmed the J-tube was patent and correctly positioned. She was managed with bowel rest, IV fluids, and anti-nausea medications including morphine and lorazepam. Her symptoms improved, and she successfully advanced from clear liquids to a soft diet. She remained afebrile without signs of infection, and urine culture showed only contamination. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue her home medications, avoid trigger foods, and follow up with her gastroenterologist.
